etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English *plodden (found only in derivative plodder), probably originally a splash through water and mud, from plodde, pludde (“a puddle”) (whence modern plud). Compare Scots plod, plodge, plodder, dialectal Dutch plodden, plodderen, dialectal German ploddern, Danish pladder (“mire”).
senses: A slow or labored walk or other motion or activity.
(intransitive) To walk or move slowly and heavily or laboriously (+ on, through, over).

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: From Middle English plod. Cognate with Danish pladder (“mire”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology 3
senses: (UK, mildly derogatory, uncountable, usually with "the") the police, police officers
(UK, mildly derogatory, countable) a police officer, especially a low-ranking one.
